sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.detail: committed first — timestamp above, before any market number
sections.markdown:
PHASE 1. No dossier exists for TINS (`data/dossiers/TINS.md` absent; fundamentals inbox empty). Load-bearing figures below are either (a) sourced commodity prices from a named public series, or (b) model assumptions triangularized from the one reported headline I could reach (TradingView company data, asof 2026-09, FY figures) — every load-bearing company-specific number is explicitly marked `PRIMARY UNAVAILABLE` pending a dossier/annual-report fetch in Phase 2. No price, quote, momentum, valuation multiple, or sell-side figure was used as a model input.

**Product-mix finding (screen factor tag tested against fundamentals):** TINS segment mix (TradingView, 2026-09) is Tin Mining, Coal Mining (subsidiary TAJ), Construction, Industrial (tin chemical, tin solder), and Other (real estate, **nickel sales**, reclamation). TINS is **tin-centric** — tin mining/smelting plus tin chemical/solder dominate; **nickel is a de minimis "Other" line, not the thesis**. The screen's `nickel_ev` factor tag does **not** match the tin-centric revenue mix. The supply-discipline/AI logic the factor intends transfers to *tin* (Indonesia controls tin supply via RKAB + export discipline; tin is the AI/data-center solder metal), but the EV/nickel demand thesis does not hold for a tin producer. I underwrite TINS as a **tin** name.

**Through-cycle tin price (sourced):** LME refined tin, 99.85% purity settlement price, World Bank Pink Sheet via IndexMundi, annual averages: 2020 17,125; 2021 32,384; 2022 31,335; 2023 25,938; 2024 30,066; 2025 34,059 USD/MT (2017-19 18.7-20.1k). 9-yr average (2017-2025) ≈ **$25,500/MT**, rounded to ~$26,000 — my through-cycle anchor. Spot Sep-2026 ≈ $54,344/MT (+56.6% y/y; late-Aug high $56,780) [TradingEconomics], driven by AI/data-center solder demand + Indonesian supply discipline (June-2026 exports 3,000t, -33% y/y; export-licence pullback; 500t unlicensed-mine metal seized). Spot is ~2.1x my anchor — that gap is cycle position (timing, not value); I underwrite at through-cycle, not spot. **~4% realization haircut vs LME** (refined-tin export/processing + Indonesian export-tax) → **through-cycle realized ≈ $25,000/MT** (assumption, method realization rule).

**Volume (PRIMARY UNAVAILABLE — assumption):** reported FY revenue Rp11.55tn (TradingView, 2026-09) ÷ through-cycle realized (~$25,000/MT ≈ Rp403m/kt at Rp16,100/USD) ≈ ~21,000 t refined-tin-equivalent, consistent with TINS's coastal smelter scale. I model **20,000 t** (assumption; primary sales-volume filing not reachable — Phase-2/dossier verify; the single largest unverified input).

**Bottom-up build (through-cycle, base case):**
- Revenue: 20,000 t × $25,000/MT ≈ $500M ≈ **Rp8.1tn tin** + ~Rp1tn coal/industrial/other ≈ **~Rp9.1tn total**.
- Cash cost: TINS is low-to-mid-quartile coastal tin dredger/smelter; through-cycle cash cost incl. royalties, depletion, RKAB/concession levies ≈ **$16,000/MT** (assumption — domestic cost PRIMARY UNAVAILABLE, flagged for war-premium energy). Cash margin ≈ $9,000/MT → ~Rp2.9tn cash EBITDA.
- Less D&A + smelting → operating ≈ Rp1.2-1.5tn; **net income ≈ Rp0.55-0.6tn (~6% through-cycle margin)** vs ~11% reported at elevated 2025 spot (cyclical, not a quality flag per se).
- **FCF:** sustaining-only capex (~Rp0.5-0.7tn/yr) + WC swing → **through-cycle FCF ≈ Rp0.3-0.4tn — thin;** multiples up at spot. Net-debt/balance-sheet PRIMARY UNAVAILABLE.
- **Dividend capacity:** MIND-ID SOE; trailing yield ~1.9%; through-cycle ~2-3% (placeholder; payout policy PRIMARY UNAVAILABLE).

**Cycle-position honesty:** this is a **through-cycle NAV setup, not a spot-momentum chase**. Upside to target comes from mean-reversion *to* the AI-re-rated incentive price; at spot ~$54k the market is already front-running that. Phase 2 must test whether entry math has room after the +285.64% 12-month screen move (momentum extension acknowledged — the market may already price the supply-discipline/price thesis; examined honestly, not assumed away).

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** TINS is an over-extended spot-tin momentum name — the re-rate (+285.64% 12m as screened) already prices the Indonesian supply-discipline and AI-solder story, leaving a hot, crowded SOE trade with no through-cycle margin of safety.
**Why wrong:** The market prices spot continuation where durable value is through-cycle NAV. Indonesia controls a dominant share of global tin supply via RKAB quotas and export licensing, and the 2024-26 record (export pullbacks, unlicensed-mine seizure, permit tightening) is genuine supply discipline, not demand speculation — the same structure as the macro desk's favored nickel tilt, transferred to tin. Tin's AI/data-center/electrification solder demand is structural and the through-cycle incentive price has re-rated up on it plus disciplined supply; at ~$25-26k/MT through-cycle vs ~$54k spot, the house method values the name on the former and treats the latter as timing. The screen-factor mismatch (nickel_ev on a tin name) may leave TINS under-owned by fundamentals-aware buyers.
**What proves us wrong:** (a) Indonesian supply discipline reverses (RKAB loosened, exports normalize) → cycle mean-reverts below the anchor; (b) through-cycle LME tin settles sustainably <$18k/MT — the AI/solder floor overestimated; (c) realized-price gap to LME widens via a new export tax beyond the modeled ~4%.

Indonesian refined-tin export volume contracted to ~3,000 t/month in June-2026 (-33% y/y) [TradingEconomics news stream] — the supply-discipline that justifies the re-rate is also the mechanism that would squeeze volume/revenue IF permit drag persists beyond pricing in; upside on price and downside on volume are two-sided.

sections.markdown: It is 2029 and this position lost 30%. The most likely reason: Indonesian supply discipline reversed (RKAB quotas loosened, exports normalized as the state monetized the price spike), tin reverted below my $26k through-cycle anchor toward the $18k floor, and TINS's thin through-cycle FCF (~Rp0.3-0.4tn) plus an SOE payout/capex surprise left the name rated on spot-cycle, not through-cycle, economics — the momentum extension having already front-run the thesis at entry.

sections.heading: Bear attack
sections.markdown:
(Drew appends verbatim; survives the Judge verdict — never edited by a later stage)

**Drew (BEAR) — VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL attack on T-INDO-TINS-001**

1. **Every load-bearing figure is unverified.** Volume (20,000 t), cash cost ($16,000/MT), FCF (~Rp0.3-0.4tn), net-debt/balance-sheet, and realized-price haircut (~4%) are all `PRIMARY UNAVAILABLE` or raw assumptions. The thesis is a model with no anchor to a single independently-filed number. Any one of these being 15-20% worse than assumed — plausible for an RKAB-constrained SOE with deferred capex and subsidy cross-subsidies — collapses the through-cycle FCF and eliminates the margin of safety. Falsifiable by: TINS annual report (idx.co.id), LK audited filing, or any buy-side diligence note.

2. **Through-cycle FCF is ~Rp0.3-0.4tn — that is the entire thesis for a ~Rp22tn market cap name.** At Rp9.1tn revenue and Rp1.2-1.5tn operating income, a single adverse line item — RKAB fee increase, energy-cost normalization, or a one-time SOE dividend surcharge — wipes the FCF. The model has zero cushion. This is not a commodity capex turnaround; it is a thinly-profitable SOE leveraged to tin price mean-reversion. Falsifiable by: FY2024 or FY2025 cash flow statement from a primary filing.

3. **+285% in 12 months means the market has already priced the supply-discipline story.** Entry is at or near the 52w high with momentum extending. The house thesis values at through-cycle ($25-26k/MT) while the market is trading at spot (~$54k/MT — 2.1x the anchor). The re-rate that Drew needs has already occurred at the entry level. What incremental buyer re-rates further from here without a documented catalyst? Falsifiable by: compare forward EPS estimates vs. current market price; if consensus shows no upgrade room, the momentum has exhausted itself.

4. **State ownership (65% government) is a structural cap on re-rating, not a durable tailwind.** MIND ID controls the dividend policy, RKAB negotiations, and export-license timing. The state extracts value through SOE levies, pension contributions, and pricing guidance that a private miner would not absorb. Indonesia's tin-supply discipline is a *policy tool*, not a market equilibrium — it can be loosened the moment Jakarta needs FX or fiscal relief. TINS is not a beneficiary of supply discipline; it is a ward of the state executing a policy. Falsifiable by: government press releases or BKPM announcements reversing RKAB permit restrictions.

5. **The realized-price haircut (4% to LME) is unverified and the wrong direction to model.** Indonesia's export tax on tin ores/concentrates was 7.5-10% in 2023-24; if a new export levy or domestic-smelt penalty is imposed above the modeled 4%, realized price drops below $24,000/MT — below the $26k through-cycle anchor. The model assumes the best case on a politically-sensitive levy. Falsifiable by: BKPM export-duty schedule or Minister of Trade decree on tin export taxation, 2025-2026.

**Verdict: MAJOR_REVISION** — the thesis has no primary-filed anchor, zero FCF cushion, and is entering a fully-extended momentum name whose re-rate has already occurred at the entry price; Phase 2 must document every load-bearing figure against a primary filing before entry can be sized.

sections.heading: Revision
sections.markdown:
**1. Unverified figures (Drew):** Drew is correct. Volume, cash cost, FCF, balance sheet — zero independently-filed anchors. Each could be 15-20% adverse; deferred capex or subsidy cross-subsidies are plausible. Without a primary filing, this thesis is a model, not an investment. Phase 2 dossier is a hard gate.

**2. Zero FCF cushion (Drew):** Drew is correct. Rp0.3-0.4tn against a ~Rp22tn market cap is effectively zero cushion. Any one of his listed shocks — RKAB fee bump, energy normalization, dividend surcharge — eliminates FCF entirely. I concede the "capex turnaround" framing overstates the asset quality; this is a marginal tin-price play on through-cycle mean-reversion, not a turn.

**3. Momentum already priced (Drew):** Drew is correct. The +285% move has already delivered the supply-discipline re-rate. The market prices spot tin; I value at through-cycle — but entry at or near the 52w high means the market has already done the work. Down_pct widened to -45% (from -35%) to reflect: entry is near the top of the range, momentum extension risk is real, and without a documented catalyst the incremental buyer is unclear.

**4. State as structural headwind (Drew):** Drew is correct. I framed RKAB/export discipline as a structural supply constraint; Drew correctly reframes it as a policy tool the state controls. MIND ID can loosen for fiscal or FX relief. I will not assume the state holds discipline — it is a thesis risk, not a tailwind, until proven otherwise by multi-year permit-data persistence.

**5. Export tax direction (Drew):** Drew is correct on direction. Actual tin-ore export tax was 7.5-10% in 2023-24. My modeled 4% haircut assumes best case on a politically-sensitive levy. I widen down_pct to -45% accordingly; any new levy above 4% reduces realized price toward or below the $26k through-cycle anchor, which alone could eliminate thesis upside. Phase 2 must pull the 2025-26 BKPM schedule before any sizing.

**Summary: MAJOR_REVISION warranted.** All five points stand. Down_pct widened to -45% (from -35%). Phase 2 hard-gate: primary filing for every load-bearing figure before sizing.

sections.heading: Judge verdict
sections.markdown:
**Verdict: PASS_REDUCED 0.50**

**Grounds:**

1. **Analyst did not concede the thesis — only down_pct.** The revision answers Drew on five-for-five: acknowledges zero FCF cushion, admits +285% momentum has already delivered the supply-discipline re-rate, concedes state as a policy risk (not tailwind), widens down_pct to -45%, and accepts Phase 2 hard-gates on primary filings. This is an honest revision. No material point was defended without acknowledgment. The thesis is diminished, not broken.

2. **Fundamentals survive at Phase 1.** Tin supply discipline is grounded in public RKAB/export data (June-2026 export pullback, seizure of 500t unlicensed-mine metal); the AI/solder demand structural call is not refuted by Drew — only its durability as a state-controlled policy tool. The through-cycle anchor at ~$26k/MT is not attacked. At Phase 1 the task is "is the fundamental premise sound enough to proceed to Phase 2 entry pricing" — it is.

3. **+285% momentum is a Phase 2 entry-pricing problem, not a Phase 1 kill.** Drew is correct that entry at or near the 52w high means the market has front-run the thesis. But Phase 1 does not set entry levels — Phase 2 does. The momentum flag is a sizing constraint, not a fundamental kill. PASS_REDUCED 0.50 reflects that half the thesis survives the Bear attack; the other half lives in Phase 2 diligence and entry timing.
